name: Thiersee
kurzbeschreibung: A picturesque village with the crystal-clear Thiersee and charming villages – a paradise for hikers and sunbathers.
beschreibung:
Overview

Thiersee is situated at an elevation of 678 meters in a sunny, expansive high valley of the Brandenberg Alps within the district of Kufstein. Covering 111 square kilometers, the municipality comprises several established hamlets including Vorderthiersee, Hinterthiersee, Mitterland, and Landl, home to approximately 3,150 residents. To the north, the valley borders Bavaria at the Ursprung Pass, while the district capital Kufstein lies merely six kilometers to the east. The centerpiece of the area is Lake Thiersee: covering around 25 hectares and reaching depths of twelve meters, this pristine alpine lake warms to a pleasant 24 degrees Celsius during summer. With its scenic lakeside promenade, public lidos, rowing boat rentals, and protected reed banks, Thiersee represents a haven of tranquility and outdoor recreation away from mass tourism.

History

Bavarian settlers colonized the high valley during the 11th century. The locality was first recorded in 1224 as 'Tyrsee' in a Bavarian land registry, with its name deriving from Old High German roots referencing game animals and indicating a ducal hunting reserve. The territory belonged to Bavaria until 1504, when Emperor Maximilian I incorporated it into Tyrol. A pivotal historical milestone occurred in 1799: faced with the threat of Napoleonic invasion, villagers pledged to stage the Passion of Christ every six years should their valley be spared devastation. Since then, the acclaimed Thiersee Passion Plays have involved virtually the entire local population. In 1926, the distinctive Passion Play House seating 1,000 spectators was built directly on the lake shore. Between 1946 and 1952, Thiersee gained fame as 'Tyrolean Hollywood', when production company Wien-Film transformed the auditorium into an active studio producing 18 feature films, including Erich Kästner's classic 'Two Times Lotte'. Architectural gems also include Saint Margaret's Church in Vorderthiersee and Saint Nicholas's Church in Hinterthiersee.

Getting There

By car, Thiersee is accessed via the Inntal Autobahn A12 by exiting at Kufstein-Nord and taking state road L37 Thierseestraße, reaching Vorderthiersee in approximately ten minutes. From Bavaria, the valley can be reached toll-free via Miesbach and Bayrischzell across the Ursprung Pass. International train services stop at Kufstein railway station, from where regular VVT regional bus lines 4046 and 4047 connect to the lakeside and outlying hamlets.

Tips

A leisurely swim at the Thiersee lido, renting a pedal boat, or strolling along the lakeside path are quintessential summer pleasures. For panoramic views, ascend Mount Pendling (1,563 meters): the hike from Schneeberg leads to the perched Kufsteiner Haus refuge, boasting spectacular vistas across the Inn Valley and the Kaiser Mountains. Experienced hikers will enjoy exploring the dramatic Glemmbachklamm gorge near Landl with its rugged footbridges. Culture lovers should check for tours of the Passion Play House or attend the historic Passion Play performances.
